newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Premier says likely to split CNA-Gallo.
newsitem.headline: Premier says likely to split CNA-Gallo.

text.p: South Africa's Premier Group Ltd said on Wednesday that it was considering unbundling its CNA-Gallo Ltd unit.
CNA-Gallo is currently trading under a cautionary announcement, warning shareholders talks are underway which may impact on its share price.
"We think it is probably going to be more appropriate to split and unbundle that business," Premier chairman Doug Band told an analysts' briefing on the publication of the group's year results.
CNA-Gallo operates a retail arm as well as the NuMetro chain of cinema's and Band said any split of the firm would divide it into separate retail and entertainment businesses.

The firm said on May 27 that a merchant bank was assessing ways to restructure the group to enable it to capitalise on its entertainment operations, which have overtaken the retail division in contribution to earnings.

Premier is a holding firm with stakes in a number of listed groups from foods firm Bonnita Ltd to drugs group Adcock Ingram Ltd. It also owns unlisted Premier Foods and drug distributor and wholesaler United Pharmaceuticals Holdings.
The total group posted year headline earnings per share of 38.0 cents, up from 28.7 last time.
Band said a restructuring at Premier Foods was now over and the arm was better equipped to cope with a still highly competitive environment.
The shake-up saw the closure of four mills, three bakeries and several depots at a cost of 100.8 million rand in lay-off charges and other restructuring costs.
Band added the new and leaner Premier Foods would help the group achieve real growth in the current year.
"A lot of medicine has been swallowed...we will deliver growth this year," Band said.
Elsewhere in the group Bonnita chairman Ian Heron said the firm, whose profits have been knocked by a milk shortage, still faced a tough six months ahead.
"For the six months we are looking at down the road it will be a very difficult trading period," he said.
Metro Cash and Carry Ltd finance director Dudley Rubin said trading at the firm had been similar so far in its current financial year to its previous one.
"At the moment trading for the first six or seven weeks of this financial year has followed a similar trend as to last year," he said.
